title: Arrested or about to be arrested
triggers: I've been arrested what are my rights
police took my father to the station
can police arrest without telling the reason

rights.plain_explanation: You must be told why you're being arrested, and you have the right to consult and be defended by a lawyer of your choice.
You must be produced before the nearest magistrate within 24 hours of arrest, not counting travel time.
When arrested without a warrant, you must be told the full grounds right away, and, for a bailable offence, that you're entitled to bail.
Police must immediately inform a relative or friend you name about the arrest and where you're held.
The arresting officer must wear a clear name tag and prepare an arrest memo, signed by a witness and by you.
During interrogation you may meet a lawyer of your choice (though not for the whole interrogation).
No one accused of an offence can be forced to be a witness against themselves.

do_now: Stay calm and don't resist; resisting gives police more powers.
Ask politely: "What are the grounds for my arrest?" and "Is this offence bailable?"
Give the name and number of a family member to be informed.
Read the arrest memo before signing it, and ask for a lawyer.
user_at_fault_cases: If there's a valid warrant or a genuine case, the arrest itself can be lawful. Your rights are about how it's done, not about avoiding it.

escalation.label: Lawyer or free legal aid
escalation.detail: Anyone in custody is entitled to free legal aid. Ask for the legal aid lawyer at the police station or court, or call 15100.

escalation.label: Magistrate
escalation.detail: Tell the magistrate when produced if your rights weren't followed. The magistrate must check this.
